questions.why: Root extracting with -p restores the archived permissions exactly.

questions.q: What does tar --exclude='*.log' do?
options: Leaves matching files out of the archive
questions.why: It's handy for skipping caches or logs when backing up.

questions.q: What is the dd command often used for?
options: Copying raw data, such as making disk images or writing ISO files to USB
questions.why: A wrong of= target can overwrite the wrong disk, so double-check it.

questions.q: What does the sync command do?
questions.why: Run it before pulling removable media if you're unsure writes have finished.

questions.q: What does the lsblk -f option add?
questions.why: It's a quick alternative to blkid for seeing filesystems.

questions.q: What does mount -o remount,rw / do?
questions.why: It's needed in rescue situations where root was mounted read-only.

questions.q: What does the noexec mount option do?
options: Prevents running programs from that filesystem
questions.why: Mounting /tmp with noexec stops attackers running dropped binaries there.

questions.q: What does the swapon --show command display?
options: Active swap devices and their usage
questions.why: mkswap prepares a device and swapon enables it.

questions.q: What is a loop device?
options: A virtual block device that lets a file be used as a disk
questions.why: mount -o loop image.iso /mnt mounts an ISO file.

questions.q: What is RAID 1?
options: Mirroring data across two or more disks
questions.why: If one disk fails, the other still holds all the data.

questions.q: What is RAID 0?
options: Striping across disks for speed, with no redundancy
questions.why: Losing any one disk loses the whole array.

questions.q: What does mdadm manage?
questions.why: cat /proc/mdstat shows the status of software RAID arrays.

questions.q: What does git clone do?
options: Copies a remote repository to your machine
questions.why: Linux admins often use git to manage scripts and configuration.

questions.q: What does the env command do when run alone?
questions.why: env VAR=value command runs one command with a modified environment.

questions.q: What does unset VAR do?
options: Removes the variable from the shell
questions.why: After unset, $VAR expands to nothing, as if it had never been set.

questions.q: What does readonly VAR do?
options: Prevents the variable from being changed or unset
questions.why: Read-only variables protect important values in scripts.

questions.q: What does the alias command with no arguments show?
questions.why: It lists every defined alias; unalias name removes one.

questions.q: What does \ls do in bash?
options: Runs ls ignoring any alias named ls
questions.why: A leading backslash bypasses aliases for that command.

questions.q: What does the locale command show?
options: Language and regional settings in use
questions.why: Settings like LANG and LC_ALL affect sorting, dates and messages.

questions.q: What does LC_ALL=C sort file do?
options: Sorts by raw byte values, ignoring locale rules
questions.why: The C locale gives fast, predictable sorting in scripts.

questions.q: What does the seq 1 5 command print?
options: The numbers 1 to 5, one per line
questions.why: seq -s, 1 5 prints them separated by commas.

questions.q: What does the expr command do?
options: Evaluates simple arithmetic and string expressions
questions.why: Bash's $(( )) arithmetic has largely replaced it.

questions.q: What does $(( 7 / 2 )) evaluate to in bash?
questions.why: Bash arithmetic uses integers, so division truncates.

questions.q: What does the bc command provide?
questions.why: echo 'scale=2; 7/2' | bc prints 3.50, unlike integer-only shell maths.

questions.q: What does the shuf command do?
questions.why: shuf randomises line order; shuf -n 1 file picks one random line.

questions.q: What does the yes command do?
options: Repeatedly prints y (or a given string)
questions.why: yes | command answers yes to every prompt.

questions.q: What does the factor command do?
options: Prints the prime factors of a number
questions.why: factor 12 prints 12: 2 2 3, listing each prime factor.

questions.q: What does the cal command show?
questions.why: cal prints a calendar for the current month; cal 2026 shows the whole year.

questions.q: What does the hexdump -C command show?
options: A file's bytes in hex alongside printable characters
questions.why: od and xxd show similar views of binary data.

questions.q: What does the iconv command do?
questions.why: iconv -f latin1 -t utf-8 fixes text saved in an old encoding.

questions.q: What does the dos2unix command do?
options: Converts Windows line endings to Unix ones
questions.why: Scripts edited on Windows often fail until their CRLF endings are fixed.
